text:
violet: heads-up: deploy-bot blocked promo for release 2026.03.21. preflight failed: artifact tarball checksum differs between registry and objectstore (gzip header mtime looks different). blocking cut.

deploy-bot: [automated] Promotion blocked: artifact-checksum-drift for artifacts.prod/release-2026-03-21.tar.gz. preflight job `upgrade-smoke-09` failed during artifact-verify. logs: https://ci.redwood/integration/1825007777/logs

sam: interesting — we've seen gzip mtime causing arbitrary checksum differences when builds are repacked by CI runners. check `gzip -l` and `tar --numeric-owner -tvf` sizes. Might be mtime in gzip header.

lee: confirms: origin object has gzip mtime 1640000000, registry copy was repacked by a proxy with current timestamp. CRC/digest changed even though payload content is same. I can recompose a canonical tarball with zeroed mtimes and reupload.

release-manager: options: A) canonicalize and reupload now (tech fix) but risks prolonging change window; B) pin to last-stable tarball digest and promote, then do canonicalize post-rollout. Which is lower risk?

sre-oncall: canonicalize+reupload is safest long-term but slower. For immediate unblock, pin to last-stable digest (sha256:deadbeef) if we can confirm all regions serve it. I can verify and annotate the old object to prevent GC.

violet: I'm leaning pin+promote to keep the change window. we should still open a follow-up to make CI produce deterministic tarballs (zero mtime, sorted entries).

sam: agreed. command to check gzip mtime quickly:
```bash
# check gzip header mtime
python -c "import gzip,sys; f=gzip.open(sys.argv[1]); print(f.mtime)" artifacts/release-2026-03-21.tar.gz
```

lee: I'll build a canonical tarball and push to staging once the immediate release is unblocked. We should also add a CI lint that fails on non-zero gzip mtime.

deploy-bot: [automated] Manual promotion queued: promote --repo prod --artifact-digest sha256:deadbeef --requester violet

sre-oncall: verified old digest sha256:deadbeef present in us-west1 and eu-west1; ap-east needs replication (ETA ~7m). Tagging current suspect object as quarantined: obj-gen:20260321-3 -> quarantined_by:sre-oncall

release-manager: vote: pin to sha256:deadbeef, promote, keep canary manual and monitor 30m, then follow-up canonicalize and republish to avoid future flaps. Also add release-note: "Temporary pin to last-stable artifact due to checksum variance; deterministic artifact pipeline to follow."

sam: running promote now and will trigger a post-promote `deployctl verify` across regions.

lee: building canonical artifact in parallel and will open PR to CI to zero-out gzip mtime and sort tar entries.

deploy-bot: [automated] Promotion started by sam. output:
2026-03-21T19:05:12Z promote: resolved digest sha256:deadbeef
2026-03-21T19:05:18Z promote: applied pin -> canary disabled pending manual enable

sre-oncall: replication to ap-east completed and checksums match sha256:deadbeef. quarantined object remains isolated.

release-manager: preflight smoke rerun passed at 19:20Z. manual canary enable scheduled for 19:30Z, monitor 30m.

violet: documenting decision and opening postmortem ticket for artifact pipeline fix. thanks all. :white_check_mark:
